site.name: Big Horn Shaft
site.location: Sugarloaf Mining District / northeast of Grand Island-Caribou district
overview: Big Horn Shaft is a documented historic mine shaft in Boulder County's Sugarloaf Mining District, northeast of the Grand Island-Caribou mining area. Federal mineral-resource material records the property as a molybdenum producer, while mapped locality data preserves a stable shaft-level identification point.

timeline.text: A federal mineral-potential synthesis reports production of molybdenite-bearing ore from pyritic quartz veins in Precambrian gneiss at the Big Horn Shaft.

moreHistory: The Bureau of Land Management's Royal Gorge Field Office mineral-potential report cites earlier Colorado and federal references for 1918 production at Big Horn Shaft and places the property just northeast of the Grand Island-Caribou district.

Mineral-locality mapping identifies Big Horn Shaft (Caribou) in the Sugarloaf Mining District near 40.01639, -105.56639. Remnant uses this mapped shaft locality for identification and does not claim that a shaft collar, headframe, foundations, or other surface remains have been field-verified or are accessible today.
A focused exact-site media search did not produce a defensible rights-cleared historical photograph for app packaging, so nearby or similarly named mine imagery was not attached.
